section.verdict: a media estate can be recomposed deterministically from its own receipts, and the provenance is legible in the artefact, not only in a manifest.

(1) the narration ran long three times (50.67 / 9.75 / 9.6 s) before landing at 8.629 s: size the line before synthesising; (2) the cleared overlay bands dropped luminance below the floor and the gate refused: fix the scene (warmer panel), never the threshold; (3) the first layout collided with the source films' own HUD text: clear a lower third.
a `proof09` brief is added to the film-production skill (size the voice first, warm the panels, clear the lower third, state provenance in-frame).

section.title: PROOF/1 — the receipted film format, de novo
section.verdict: a film format can carry the laboratory's rules as FIELDS, not as habits; the same spec + the same assets render the same bytes.

the format has no source-drift check: the renderer reads and burns a source's sha256 but does not refuse when a source no longer matches the spec's record. A film can therefore be rendered from a changed asset and still pass.
add an optional `expected_sha256` to each beat; the renderer must refuse on mismatch. Until then, the receipt cites the spec, not the asset.

section.title: ORACLES/09 — the instrument panel
section.verdict: a proof can make the apparatus its subject, and the panel's gaps are legible in-frame: the format behaved as designed.
the in-frame digest was labelled `sha256` while showing 32 hex (a truncation); the hash was right, the label was wrong.

footer now `sha256[:32]`; format law 4 states the truncation; CHAIN/09 re-rendered so the live artefact matches the rule. Not verified: browser playback; whether the three 0-test oracles should be tested next (recorded as the obvious follow-up).

section.title: Studios and camera shots — the resource inventory
section.verdict: the camera and state vocabularies are finite and nameable; a film can be specified without inventing a shot.
the inventory itself exposes two live defects: v2's output is too dark (live film lum 11.08) and v3 runs at ~12 s/frame.
the inventory is now a published resource; choosing a studio is a lookup, not a recollection. Follow-up recorded: brighten v2's scene defaults, and decide whether v3 is worth its render budget.

section.title: SHOWREEL/09 — the demonstration of what our assets make
section.verdict: the estate's film kinds are finite and each has a live example; a showreel can be assembled from them in one deterministic render.
the voice line ran long twice (10.19 s, 8.86 s) and the format's own `max_seconds` guard refused both: size the line before synthesising.
nothing to change in the format (the guard worked); recorded as the reason the brief says 'size the voice first'. Not verified: browser playback of the showreel.

section.title: GAIT/09 — the best raster on the saved gait
section.verdict: the RTX raster renders the assembled CAD from the SAVED trace with no keyframes, and the camera follows the walker. Visual check: a connected humanoid (head, torso, arms, legs), not scattered geometry.
the renderer's own meta labels wall time as `seconds: 99.9`; the real duration is 9.000 s (ffprobe). Field-naming bug in `rtx_asimov.py`.

recorded; the meta should say `wall_s`, not `seconds`. Rasters ranked: tinycuda 49 fps @1M tris (the oracle) · rtx_raster 77 ms @1.007M tris (depth-correct) · tinygpu 71.6 ms/frame · æRTXrender (CDP) · emoji_scene.

section.title: The three untested oracles — now tested
section.verdict: the time-axis, ledger and plugin oracles are deterministic and their refusals are reachable; a green grade now means something.

two filmmemory tests were written against a guessed chain shape and failed honestly; the tests were corrected to the real API (append-built chains, drift keyed on kind='film'), not the API bent to the test.
the three oracles are tested; ORACLES/09 can be re-cut so the zeroes become 15 / 9 / 6.

section.title: tinyPOLICY — mobility.foundation command and control
section.verdict: the governance primitives already existed in tinypython (sense, arm, disarm, presence, deadman_gate); tinyPOLICY names and ledgers them rather than reinventing them. `exec stand` refuses with three rules; `gate simulate` allows.
two tests assumed `exec` was a verb and `presence` was a rule code; the surface says otherwise (exec is the protocol action; the rules are ACT-001 / AUTH-002 / DEAD-001). Tests corrected to the code.
mobility.foundation now has a tested C2; point it at a trace and cite its ledger like any other receipt.

section.title: tinyONNX — the policy oracle; five policies, two runnable
section.verdict: the policy set is measurable, and the refusal is a measurement (78/12, 45/12), not an assumption.
the first run crashed on a duplicated argparse subparser; fixed by registering each subparser once.
'test them all' is now a contract check first: 2 of 5 run, 3 refuse.

section.title: tinyVISION — supervision for the robot policy
section.verdict: the supervision we already trust on films grades the policy's picture, and the picture agrees with the physics.
the first track used DetectorMovimiento and returned 227 tracks; the `caja` field does not exist (it is `xyxy`); the renderer needs CuPy (C:/gpu/Scripts/python.exe) and --model-dir tinygpu/model.
the policy now has a visual instrument: a trace that claims success while the film shows a frozen body would be caught.

section.title: The loop closes — tinyLAB, and the video that proves it
section.verdict: the laboratory can observe itself, find a broken instrument, and instruct its own repair; the repair was re-measured green.
the self-study's first run was red, and the red was real (a namespace shadowing bug), not a flaky test.
the new video is the one the lab asked for: the loop, closed.

section.title: VERBS/09 — the mobility verbs, done and refused
section.verdict: the body does five verbs, measured; the other four are governed.
the voice line was sized wrong three times (11.24 s, 10.34 s, 8.99 s against an 8.6 s max); the renderer refused each time, correctly. Sized to the picture at ~0.43 s/word.
the verb surface is now a film, not a table.

section.title: The post — "The film is an instrument"
section.verdict: the improvement is publishable as a surface, not a claim: every number on the page is one we measured this session and can re-derive.
the first live check returned 200 with size_download 0 (a curl artifact); the real bytes were 11,251 and matched.
the estate now has a post that states the method and its limits in the same page.

section.title: The camera fix — the film becomes a teacher
section.verdict: the traversal is in the picture, and the number that proves it (21 -> 589 px) is measured, not asserted.
the free-root camera pulled back far enough that the accent blob fell under the tracker's area_min (2000); at 300 it tracks 1 blob over 216 frames. A detection floor is a parameter, not a constant.
the film is a teacher of trajectory. The next instrument is the inverse: film -> path.

section.title: asimov pet — its own gaits, and a receipt
section.verdict: the mascot walks and turns with the policy's own gaits, and the sheet carries the hash that proves which traces made it.
the first install used the output dir name as the pet id (`asimov-pet`); the id must stay `asimov-cad`, so it was re-rendered under the right slug.
the pet is receipted and gait-faithful; the next improvement is the lab link (pet state derived from tinylab's own verdict).

section.title: DOM awareness — the companion reads the page
section.verdict: the pet reads the document and reports what it found, with a fingerprint; the read is a measurement, not a claim.
the first observer watched its own HUD writes (fingerprint moved fa734705 -> 957daa02 between calls); and the boot write was swallowed by a renderer-not-ready throw inside setState. Both fixed.
the companion is DOM-aware; the same read works on any surface, so the next step is injecting it over CDP rather than only on its own page.

section.title: The companion's CAD was missing — now it renders
section.verdict: the companion is a working surface again: CAD + DOM awareness.
the page was silently dead for as long as it has been published; nothing in the repo recorded that `scene/` was missing.
a web-sized CAD (6.1 MB) now ships with the surface, and the simplification is a parameter with the trade-off measured.

section.title: actor:// — the robots are actors
section.verdict: a script drives the actor's move, word and camera; the motion is the policy's, not a pose.
`--dry` first demanded the clips exist; a dry run validates the script and must not render. Fixed.
the cast is data: add an actor by adding a cast entry and traces.

section.title: tinyGPUBOT — the actor instrument
section.verdict: the cast is data and the performance is receipted; the actor layer and the bot are separate, so a script can be performed by any governed bot.
two tests pointed ROOT one level short, so the trace path did not exist and `cast` refused correctly; the TESTS were wrong, not the code.
the robot is now a named, governed, receipted actor: tinyGPUBOT.

section.title: The mixture, performed
section.verdict: the mixture's cast is data; each body performs its own verb rather than replaying one walk.
the compositor's first filter string put the ffmpeg ':' separators OUTSIDE the f-strings (a syntax error at line 70); moved inside.
the mixture is now a governed performance: five actors and one authority, receipted.

section.title: The mixture, composited — and an honest WARN
section.verdict: the mixture's cast is data, every move is a policy trace, and the authority is a first-class panel rather than a caption.

the first composite FAILED luminance (19.19): the gate card was near-black and dragged the grid's mean under the floor. Fixed the SCENE (warm (22,19,13) panel + a gold grid), never the threshold. Also: drawtext cannot take a non-ASCII font path - the font is staged to an ASCII temp dir and the drive colon is escaped.
the mixture is a governed performance surface: five actors and one authority, composited and receipted.

section.title: The post, updated
section.verdict: the published post and the estate agree; the correction is on the record rather than quietly dropped.
the first live fetch returned the OLD bytes (11,359) for three checks; the blob was authoritative, the CDN lagged. Re-checked until equal.
the surface now tells the whole story, including the retraction.

section.verdict: the grading instrument had a frame bug; fixing it changes every verdict, and the honest outcome is 'no retirement'.
my own published finding was the bug. The film retracts it.
tinypython's per-segment verdict is body-frame; the 'body-frame finding' becomes the 'body-frame VERDICT finding'. ---

section.title: microduck:// — the governed SDK, same shape as asimov://
section.verdict: the governed layer is real and exercised end to end, and the gate refuses motion without an armed approval.

`duckctl` and `robotctl` are not installed on this host, and `scripts/duck-sim` is a `#!/bin/sh` harness that cannot run under this Windows bash (`[WinError 5]`). So every live transport is **absent, and the protocol says so** rather than reporting a pass. The sim twin needs WSL/Linux or a macOS host.
any Pollen robot with an official daemon + IPC now has a template: wrap the daemon's own verbs, add the gate and the receipt, expose `sim`.

section.title: Provenance stills, a GIF audit, and two self-corrections
section.verdict: the ontology taxonomy renders deterministically to still + GIF; the tinyMuJoCo claims (doctor, 21 tests, ledger chain, film hash) survive a re-run; the GIF tests would catch real drift.
two of my own claims were wrong (file path; transient count), and a GIF collapsed to 17 frames before the continuous-motion fix. All three were found and corrected in-session rather than shipped.

a still/GIF may now be drawn from a live manifest instead of a prompt; the rule is read the artifact at render time, never repeat a count from a doc. Nothing in this section was committed or pushed — the record itself is the artifact.
